subject.title: Feature: Surface cron job name / session label in /status and statusline

question: Should the remaining CLI/TUI status-label work adopt the open conflicting fork PR, ask for a new narrow replacement, or defer behind a broader status-label design?
rationale: The user problem is real, but the visible identifier precedence and terminal-sanitization requirements affect operator-facing status surfaces, and an open conflicting fork PR already claims the issue.

options.title: Request narrow replacement
options.body: Keep this issue open, close or supersede the conflicting fork PR, and ask for a focused patch that propagates sanitized labels through the shared status contract while preserving raw keys.

options.title: Adopt the fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer repair the existing fork branch, but require conflict resolution, terminal-safety changes, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Defer to broader attribution
options.body: Leave the CLI/TUI display gap open until maintainers settle the larger JSON/status attribution shape, at the cost of continued UUID-heavy status output.

recommendation.title: Request narrow replacement
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, close or supersede the conflicting fork PR, and ask for a focused patch that propagates sanitized labels through the shared status contract while preserving raw keys.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining work sits in the status summary/types/renderer path where this person has recent adjacent history.
